overview-s000.title: What You Will Learn in This Workshop
overview-s000.markdown:
This hands-on workshop is for FP&A / finance / corporate planning professionals who want to rethink Excel-centered budgeting, and for Power BI / Fabric implementation teams. It is designed for an in-person group of **10–20 workshop participants**.

01 / Build a plan

Allocate company-wide targets and connect field input, locking, comments, and approvals.

02 / Compare assumptions

Use Optimizer, statistical forecasting, and scenarios to distinguish numbers that meet a target from operationally sound assumptions.

03 / Verify saved results

Learn to write back to Fabric SQL and verify saved values, not just success logs.

04 / Clarify implementation requirements

Review how actuals and plans are presented, permissions, capacity, and billing, then define success criteria to measure in your own PoC.
**Start here:** [Getting started](#はじめ方) / [Lab list and duration](#ラボ一覧) / [Participant HTML](https://github.com/yang-jiayi/FabricPlanWorkshop/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/workshop-presentation.html) / [Usage guide](docs/PRESENTATION-GUIDE-JA.md) / [Glossary](#財務会計用語)

overview-s001.title: Workshop Objectives
overview-s001.markdown:
Using the fictional Harborlight Provisions Co. as a case study, this workshop helps participants build an annual plan in Fabric Planning from data scattered across Excel and check its input assumptions and saved results. The workshop combines product demonstrations with a review of the processes, data, stakeholders, and PoC success criteria participants may test in their own organizations.

Sample operations do not demonstrate performance, cost savings, accounting correctness, or production suitability.

overview-s002.title: Architecture
overview-s002.markdown:
Importing `Northwind_FMCG.pbix` creates the report and semantic model. The main Plan connects to one model. Lab04 writes its Forecast values to Fabric SQL, but they are not automatically reflected in the existing report or semantic model. ```mermaid flowchart LR PBIX["Northwind_FMCG.pbix"] --> REPORT["Existing report"] PBIX --> MODEL["Semantic model"] MODEL --> PLAN["Main Plan
Labs 01?06 / 08"] PLAN --> SHEETS["Planning sheets / Intelligence"] PLAN -.->|Writeback| SQL["Fabric SQL"] SQL -.->|After explicit connection| DOWNSTREAM["Downstream analysis"] ``` **Dashed lines indicate SQL writeback and downstream analysis after SQL tables are explicitly connected.** Lab09 is a separate advanced lab. Parts 3?5 using a synthetic CSV were exercised in Fabric, including Warehouse verification, Lakehouse Delta, Ontology / Graph, and some Data Agent questions. Q4 / Q4a returned `SQLCandidatesFailedFilterError`. The Warehouse is used to verify Decimal values; the Ontology Graph source is the Lakehouse managed Delta table. See [Lab09](labs/09-variance-analyst.md) / [Data flow](assets/diagrams/lab-flow.md) / [Lab09 architecture diagram](assets/diagrams/lab09-variance-analyst.md). **Referencing and copying are different.** A plan series referenced with From Sheets receives changes from its source. In contrast, the editable copy in Lab03 does not automatically synchronize with the original sheet. In Intelligence as well, configure From Sheets inputs and actuals from the semantic model as distinct sources. [Data configuration guide](data/README.md)

Lab09 is an additional advanced exercise (45–60 minutes, excluding data preparation) and is not included in the core path or the 180-minute in-person workshop. Adding both Lab07 and Lab09 brings the estimate to 240–255 minutes. These are the sum of the time estimates for each lab, not a guarantee of completion including environment setup or wait times. overview-s006.title: Financial Terminology
overview-s006.markdown: The participant and instructor HTML editions explain financial terms at their first use in the articles and include a glossary with sources. Open the [glossary in the participant HTML](docs/workshop-presentation.html#glossary-s000). See the [HTML usage guide](docs/PRESENTATION-GUIDE-JA.md) for annotation behavior and controls. These definitions explain terminology; they do not establish that the sample calculations comply with accounting standards.

overview-s004.title: Facilitation and Usage Notes
overview-s004.markdown:
**The default format is for the instructor to handle design / configuration while participants experience input / review / approval.** The [Facilitator Guide](docs/FACILITATOR-GUIDE.md) includes advance preparation, a 180-minute schedule, pair roles, recovery steps for common problems, and a PoC planning worksheet.
When product availability or screens differ from the materials The procedures and images include content checked in the author's Fabric environment in October–November 2026. Fabric UI and features change. **This does not assert that every individual feature, region, or tenant has the same availability.** Before the workshop, the instructor should rehearse in the actual account and environment and check the [official overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/plan/overview), [prerequisites](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/plan/overview-prerequisites), and [known limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/plan/overview-limitations).
Choosing capacity and permissions for the group size Do not infer concurrent-use performance or cost from F2, the smallest capacity. Billing roles (Planner / Stakeholder / Viewer) are separate from workspace roles. Assign owners for capacity and costs. Use the activity-based estimates in the [Facilitator Guide](docs/FACILITATOR-GUIDE.md). Do not assume model RLS, input values, comments, and KPI visibility have identical scopes; refer to the limitations and verification steps in [Lab08](labs/08-sizing-and-governance.md).
Can the P&L model be used for production decisions? [Lab05](labs/05-pl-models-and-scenarios.md) distinguishes simple averages from quantity-weighted unit prices, annual from monthly values, and measures from row models. Do not treat the simplified exercise P&L model as a complete accounting model; separately verify your organization's definitions, aggregation granularity, signs for deductions, and expense scope.
